sources_inspected.label: National Archives, NARA Bulletin 2015-04 Appendix B (accessed 2026-08-25)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The NARA appendix supports descriptive, consistent file naming and placing dates or version numbers in a consistent location.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: Its federal records-management guidance is used as an administrative naming principle only, not as a mineral-rights requirement or legal-retention rule.

sources_inspected.label: NIST, FIPS 180-4 Secure Hash Standard (accessed 2026-08-25)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: NIST FIPS 180-4 specifies secure hash algorithms that generate message digests for messages or files.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article limits an optional SHA-256 digest to byte-change detection and does not claim identity, authorship, authenticity, completeness, legal validity, or fraud detection.

sources_inspected.label: Texas Attorney General, How to Avoid Home Improvement Scams (accessed 2026-08-25)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The Texas Attorney General page supports the general consumer practice of reading written terms and keeping copies.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: It is expressly labeled general consumer guidance from a different transaction context, not mineral-rights law, contract interpretation, or a deadline rule.

sources_inspected.label: Texas Attorney General, How to Spot and Report Phone Scams (accessed 2026-08-25)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The Texas Attorney General page identifies pressure and limited-time tactics as general consumer warning signs.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses that point only to support preserving communications and asking bounded follow-up questions, not to label a mineral-rights offer or party fraudulent or illegitimate.
